The test

What each level asks

The HSK is run by Chinese Testing International (CTI) for the Center for Language Education and Cooperation (中外语言交流合作中心), which writes its papers and syllabus. Its new format, which CTI calls HSK 3.0, has three stages and nine levels: levels 1 to 6 are separate tests, so you can take any of them without the one below, and levels 7 to 9 are one advanced exam that places you at level 7, 8 or 9.

CTI launches the new levels 1 to 6 worldwide on 13 December 2026. Sittings before then use the format of 2009, which has different parts and timings; Glossa's papers follow the new format only. Levels 3 to 6 have a separate speaking test, and HSK 7–9 has speaking and translation inside the exam.

LevelThe real testIn Glossa's papers

HSK 3Listening 30 items in about 23 minutes, reading 30 in 30, writing 10 in 20. Characters only, apart from the pinyin over the gaps of the first writing task.Listening has 15 items in 12 minutes, with every part kept. Reading and writing are full length.
HSK 4Listening 32 items in about 20 minutes, reading 32 in 30, writing 6 in 25: five sentences about pictures and a short text of at least 80 characters. No pinyin from here on.Listening has 16 questions in 10 minutes and reading 16 in 15. Writing is full length.
HSK 5Listening 35 items in about 25 minutes, reading 35 in 35, writing 2 in 40: a picture story of at least 100 characters and an essay of at least 200.Listening has 18 questions in 13 minutes and reading 16 in 20. Writing is full length.
HSK 6Listening 40 items in about 30 minutes, reading 40 in 40, writing 2 in 45: a practical text of at least 150 characters and an essay of at least 300.Listening and reading have 20 questions each, in 15 and 20 minutes. Writing is full length.
HSK 7–9Listening 40 items in about 33 minutes, reading 40 in 50, writing 2 in 55, translation 4 in 42, speaking 5 in about 20. Scores

How the new HSK is scored

The scoring of the new format is only partly published.

  • HSK 1 to 6: CTI and the Center for Language Education and Cooperation have not published section maximums, totals or pass marks for the new format. The figures of the 2009 format do not apply to it.
  • HSK 7–9: each of the five sections gets a report score from 0 to 100, and the result is given as level 7, 8 or 9, or as below level 7. CTI publishes no cut scores for the three levels and no pass mark.
  • Score reports of HSK 6 and HSK 7–9 are valid for two years, CTI states.

Vocabulary

How many words each level asks for

The HSK syllabus published in November 2025, in force from July 2026, lists these vocabularies, counting the words of the levels below:

  • HSK 1: 300 words
  • HSK 2: 500 words
  • HSK 3: 1,000 words
  • HSK 4: 2,000 words
  • HSK 5: 3,600 words
  • HSK 6: 5,400 words
  • HSK 7–9: 11,000 words

Honest limits

How the practice papers differ from the real test

  • No HSK score is given. A section's result is the share of points you got. Glossa does not convert it into an HSK score or a level, or say whether you would pass.
  • Listening and reading are shorter from HSK 4 on. They have about half the questions of the real test, and at HSK 3 listening does, with every part kept and the time cut to match. HSK 2 is full length, and writing is full length at every level that has it.
  • There is no speaking. The papers leave out the separate speaking tests of HSK 3 to 6, and the speaking and spoken translation of HSK 7–9.
  • Pictures and charts are described in words. Where the real paper shows pictures, the options or prompts describe them; at HSK 7–9 the chart is a table.
  • Characters are typed, not written by hand, so the papers test choosing the right character rather than writing its strokes.
  • Recordings can be replayed, which the real test does not allow, so play each one once and then answer.
  • Words can be tapped for their meaning while you practise; the real test allows no dictionary.

Questions

Common questions

Is Glossa connected with the HSK?
No. Glossa is not connected with Chinese Testing International or the Center for Language Education and Cooperation. The papers follow their published sample papers and syllabus, with original content.
Do the papers follow the old HSK or the new one?
The new format (HSK 3.0), which CTI launches for levels 1 to 6 on 13 December 2026. The 2009 format used before then has different parts, timings and scores, and Glossa's papers do not model it. HSK 7–9 has had the same structure since 2022.
Which level should I practise for?
Each level's papers are written for learners who have finished the matching tier of the course: HSK 1 after Tier 2, HSK 2 after Tier 3, and so on up to HSK 7–9 after Tier 8. The placement test shows where you are.
What is free?
The whole Chinese course from pinyin to HSK 7–9, the grammar reference and word practice are free. The HSK practice papers, conversation practice, stories and the other extras are part of Premium.
